claims.statement: Tom Allen said he had planned to go to Mexico to see the Maher-Fitzsimmons fight, but stayed home after Jim Hall wrote that he would be a sucker to risk his money on the same deal as at Hot Springs.
claims.excerpt: I was goin' down to see the fights, but Jim 'All wrote me an' said I would be a sucker

claims.statement: Tom Allen was one of the St. Louis pugilists quoted in February 1896.
claims.excerpt: Tom Allen, Dutch Neal, Fred Watkins and other lights in the St. Louis pugilistic firmament

claims.statement: Tom Allen said he did not know the first principle of bull fighting but believed any so-called sport that calls for dead horses and bulls is no sport at all.
claims.excerpt: But he believes that any so-called sport that calls for dead horses and bulls is no sport at all.

quotes.speaker: Tom Allen
quotes.text: I was goin' down to see the fights, but Jim 'All wrote me an' said I would be a sucker to put up me coin an' take chances on gettin' th' same deal that was put up at 'Ot Springs.
quotes.topic: why he stayed home from the Mexico fight

quotes.speaker: Tom Allen
quotes.text: Th' bloody papers do all the fightin' now, instead of th' fighters doin' it. We never used to fight in th' papers. If we didn't fight th' papers roasted us.

notes: Dialect quotes. 'Jim 'All' read as Jim Hall. Soapy Burns mentions 'Lootenant Allen's wagon'; it is not clearly Tom Allen, so it is not recorded.
